learning_outcomes.text: The student predicts the result of existing PHP and JS code without the help of a server or other software program.

The student is able to understand an ERD diagram and design one independently based on functional requirements. He/she can convert this diagram into a concrete database. He/she understands how different tables are linked and can also correctly link them using foreign keys and associative tables.
The student writes SQL queries to retrieve and display all requested data from a database and predicts the result of an SQL query for a given database.
The student develops a working web application with an associated database.
The student deals ethically with source files, source code, and libraries found online or in textbooks.
The student develops a robust data model for his/her web application, translates this into an ERD diagram, and converts it into a database.
The student uses the correct technologies for the different parts of the application.
The student incorporates security to prevent misuse of the application.
The student tests the application during the development process with a view to delivering a successful working whole that meets the stated requirements.
The student makes a realistic and effective plan for his/her own activities and processes. He/she delivers the project by the proposed deadline.

syllabus_topics: Dynamic website capabilities vs. static websites
Webserver and database server (MySQL) for data storage and retrieval
Serverscripts (PHP) for dynamic websites and web applications (search actions, customized information retrieval, service registration)
Asynchronous loading of larger data packets for optimized user experience
Correct database construction for web applications
Supporting exercises for familiarity with theoretical technologies
Development of a self-developed, dynamic website or web application using an underlying database system (MySQL)
assessment_rules: The course is evaluated based on two activities: a theory exam and a lab exam. Each activity evaluates separate learning outcomes. The theory exam evaluates learning outcomes (1), (2), and (3). The lab exam evaluates learning outcomes (4) - (10). If a student scores <7 on either evaluation activity, the student can achieve a maximum of 9/20 for the entire course. For re-sits, there are partial transfers for successful partial results (Theory and Lab, within the academic year). For the lab re-sit, the student must create an improved version of their webshop and contact the lecturer to understand the shortcomings of the first submission.
